# BACTERIAL MENINGITIS (WITHOUT GRAM STAIN RESULTS)

Once a diagnosis of acute bacterial meningitis is considered likely, antimicrobials should be initiated as soon as possible. Two blood cultures should be drawn. Lumbar puncture (LP) should be performed in nearly all patients to obtain cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) for establishing diagnosis and determining infectious organism/susceptibility. Adjust antimicrobial regimen to optimize therapy and treatment duration based on pathogen once isolated.

Intravenous dexamethasone therapy improves outcomes for meningitis with Streptococcus pneumoniae and is recommended for empirical treatment of all community acquired cases that might be associated with S. pneumoniae.

Dexamethasone must be given before (1 to 20 minutes) with antimicrobials.

If meningococcal meningitis is identified, antimicrobial prophylaxis should be considered for close contacts. Contact Infectious Diseases/Epidemiology for advice and assistance.

# Consult Infectious Diseases

Therapy:
## Step 1 of Treatment

Dexamethasone 10 mg IV q6h ($) for 4 days

(Discontinue if isolated pathogen is not S. pneumoniae)

## Step 2 of Treatment, Select One of the Following:

## Treatment for Adults < 50 Years Without Alcoholism, Debilitating Disease, or Any Other Condition Associated with Impaired Cellular Immunity.

Preferred:

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h ($) M <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) R

Alternative:

Assessment of beta-lactam reaction

Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h ($$) R <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg q12h ($) R

## Treatment for Adults >= 50 Years or With Alcoholism, Debilitating Disease, or Impaired Cellular Immunity. Listeria Monocytogenes is One Important Pathogen.

Preferred:

Ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h ($$) R <AND> ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h ($) M <AND>
vancomycin 15mg/kg q12h ($) [R]

Alternative:

Assessment of beta-lactam reaction

Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h ($$) [R,O] ] <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]
Inpt: ORZID2 GMENU BACT MENING W/O GRM STAIN RES
